chunks: Ali, from his father, from Haroun Bin Al Jahm, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

My father looked at a man and with him was his son, walking, and the son was leaning upon the arm of the father. So my father (peace be upon him) did not speak to him in aversion to him until he separated from the world.

key_terms.مَقْتاً: aversion or dislike, used here to indicate speaking to avoid distraction

ai.seo_question: What is the etiquette of interacting with parents or elders when they are walking or occupied?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) observed a son leaning on his father's arm, a posture often associated with youthful arrogance or ingratitude, yet he refrained from immediate rebuke to avoid causing the father distraction or physical stumble. This incident highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *hilm* (forbearance) and the subtle, non-verbal correction of social manners, illustrating how the Imams prioritized preserving the dignity and focus of the elder over immediate verbal admonition. The silence serves as a profound lesson in observing the nuances of family dynamics and the weight of parental authority in daily interactions.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Haroun Bin Al Jahm, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> looked at a man and with him was his son, walking, and the son was leaning upon the arm of the father. So my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> did not speak to him in aversion (so not to distract him) to him until he<sup>asws</sup> separated from the world’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali has narrated from his father from Harun ibn al-Jahm from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sulayman from abu la’ far (a.s.) who has said the following:
“Once, my father saw a man walking with his son who was leaning against his father’s arm. My father in dislike never spoke to him until he left this world.”
